text:
Olga: Starting a slow-staged rollout for v3.0.0. Target 0->5->15 over 30m. Change window 08:00-09:00 UTC. Starting with AZ-a slice (multi-AZ aware). /deploy release=v3.0.0 percent=5 slice=az-a

deploy-bot: [08:00:02] Deploy started: v3.0.0 -> canary 5% (AZ-a). CI checks passed. Link: https://deploy.internal/r/3823456789

Ben: watching AZ-a metrics. If p95 > 250ms or errors > 0.7% hold and consult SRE. Also watch cross-AZ failover count.

Maya: QA: running a quick smoke on top prompts; will post if any content regressions.

DevOps: Noted. We've got a minor infra kernel rollout in AZ-b at 07:50 but AZ-a should be untouched. Still, watch host churn.

deploy-bot: [08:12:10] Scheduled ramp: 5% -> 15% in 18m. Safety checks: KV cache pressure=low, OOM risk=low, AZ-saturation=ok.

Ben: p95 AZ-a = 265ms and errors = 0.9% at 08:14. Cross-AZ retries spiking, likely causing tail. Panel: https://grafana.internal/d/az/canary-az-a

Olga: Hmm. That's over our threshold. @sre-oncall can you run the az-isolate script and check node churn/packets? If it's infra-caused we may pin AZ-a to stable and continue other AZs.

sre-oncall: Running `./ops/az_isolate --az=az-a --past=15m` now. Early results: 3 node restarts in az-a starting 08:11; network flaps reported by CNI plugin. I recommend pausing the AZ-a ramp and pinning AZ-a to v2.9.9 to keep traffic healthy.

Maya: QA: my smoke tests show increased latency but no functional regressions. Looks like infra instability.

Olga: OK. Decision: pause AZ-a ramp and pin to v2.9.9. Keep global canary running for other AZs (we'll exclude az-a). If we see cascading cross-AZ retries we consider a full rollback. Any objections?

Ben: +1 to pin AZ-a. We want to avoid full rollback if it's infra. Also recommend enabling fallback model-variant for az-a to avoid cache cold-start when we re-route traffic.

DevOps: confirming network team is investigating CNI plugin flaps; will post ETA.

Olga: @deploy-bot pin-az az=az-a version=v2.9.9 reason="CNI network flaps and node restarts"

deploy-bot: [08:16:12] Pin applied: az-a pinned to v2.9.9. Global canary remains at 9% excluding az-a. Automatic rollback not triggered (manual pin). Links: https://deploy.internal/pins/3823456789

cs: Drafting release note: "AZ-a slice paused at ~9% due to infra network flaps; pinned to v2.9.9 while investigation continues." Adding to draft: https://docs.internal/releases/v3.0.0-draft

Maya: QA will run a focused regression against v3.0.0 in an az-a-like env once infra is stable, especially cache-heavy prompts. ETA 40m.

Ben: Setting a timer: if we don't have infra stabilization + QA signoff in 50m we'll schedule a staged rollback for AZ-a at 09:05 UTC. If infra fixes earlier we can unpin and do a 2% cautious resume.

sre-oncall: Network team reports fix attempt at 08:28; watching for stabilization. Also will check if any kernel updates coincided with restarts.

DevOps: Network team patched CNI at 08:29 and rolled a fix to az-a; nodes appear stable at 08:33. Monitoring for 10m.

deploy-bot: [08:33:55] Note: safety re-check passed for az-a (post-fix). Pin still applied. Use `/deploy unpin az=az-a` to remove manual pin after approvals. Auto-rollback timer still scheduled for 09:05 UTC if not cleared.

Maya: Running QA regression now in az-a-like infra. Posting green/reds in thread.

Maya: QA result: reg-suite done, all critical tests green, perf tests show p95 back to baseline ~130ms in the test environment. Requesting +1 from SRE to unpin and resume at 2% step.

sre-oncall: Observability looks stable for 12m with no further restarts. +1 to unpin and resume with cautious step. Recommend keeping fallback model-variant enabled for the first step.

Olga: Vote check: Ben? DevOps? Need explicit +1 to unpin az-a and resume rollout.

Ben: +1.

DevOps: +1. Nodes stable.

Olga: OK. @deploy-bot unpin-az az=az-a and resume percent=2 step=2 reason="infra fixed + QA green + SRE +1"

deploy-bot: [08:43:30] Action: Unpin applied for az-a. Resuming canary: adding 2% to global canary excluding AZs with active pins. Current global canary now 11.9% incl. az-a step. Safety: enabling fallback-model-variant for az-a for first 10m.

cs: Updating release notes: removed the previous pin note and adding: "AZ-a resumed under cautious step after infra fix and QA signoff; fallback variant enabled temporarily."

Olga: Thanks team. We'll keep the thread live until the change window closes. If any regressions appear we may abort and execute the scheduled rollback for az-a at 09:05.

deploy-bot: [08:44:10] Reminder: change window ends 09:00 UTC. Auto-rollback timer for az-a cleared. Use `/deploy rollback region=az-a` to force rollback if needed.
